title: Keritot 11
description: The espoused maidservant: why she is flogged and he brings the guilt offering, what “redeemed and not redeemed” means to Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya and Aḥerim, a corrupt-seeming baraita that Rav Sheshet keeps, the close of chapter 2, and the opening mishna of chapter 3 on witnesses who say “you ate forbidden fat.”
topics: 🔍 Bikkoret: she is flogged and he is not; reading the verses (Rabbi Yitzḥak) or assessing the lashes (Rav Ashi)
⚖️ When the woman is flogged the man brings an offering: Rava reads the order of the verse
🌾 Rabbi Yitzḥak: only a non-virgin maidservant, from harifot, groats; Rav Ḥisda on the priests in Ezra
📜 “Redeemed and not redeemed”: Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Yishmael, Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya and Aḥerim
👥 Mishna: a minor, one sleeping, one unwitting; and why with the maidservant even the adult and the awake are exempt
🧩 A tanna before Rav Sheshet: “they rendered one who completes like one who begins,” read through “lies carnally”
📖 Hadran: chapter 2, Arba’a Meḥusarei Kappara, ends; chapter 3, Amru Lo, begins
🧾 Witnesses who say “you ate forbidden fat”: Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis, one witness, and silence

a2.he: אֵיזוֹ שִׁפְחָה? כֹּל שֶׁחֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה״, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: זוֹ הִיא שִׁפְחָה וַדָּאִית. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת מְפוֹרָשׁוֹת, וְשִׁיּוּר אֵין לָנוּ אֶלָּא חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין.

a3.he: גְּמָ׳ מְנָלַן דְּהִיא לָקְיָ[א] וְהוּא לָא לָקֵי? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בִּקּוֹרֶת תִּהְיֶה״ – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהִיא לוֹקָה. יָכוֹל שְׁנֵיהֶן לוֹקִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״תִּהְיֶה״ – הִיא לוֹקֶה וְהוּא אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה.

a4.he: וּמִנַּיִן דְּהָדֵין ״בִּקּוֹרֶת״ לִישָּׁנָא דְּמַלְקוּת הוּא? אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: ״תְּהֵא בֵּקָרָאֵי״, כִּדְתַנְיָא: גְּדוֹל הַדַּיָּינִין מַקְרִא, שֵׁנִי מוֹנֶה, שְׁלִישִׁי אוֹמֵר: הַכֵּהוּ. רַב אָשֵׁי אוֹמַר: ״בְּבִיקּוּר תִּהְיֶה״, כְּדִתְנַן: אֵין אוֹמְדִין אוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא מַכּוֹת הָרְאוּיוֹת לְהִשְׁתַּלֵּשׁ.

a5.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָאִשָּׁה לוֹקָה – הָאִישׁ מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן, אֵין הָאִשָּׁה לוֹקָה – אֵין הָאִישׁ מֵבִיא קׇרְבָּן. מְנָלַן? אָמַר רָבָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע וְהִיא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חוּפְשָׁה לֹא נִתַּן לָהּ״.

a6.he: מִכְּדִי עַד הָכָא בְּאִישׁ קָא מִשְׁתַּעֵי קְרָא, נִכְתּוֹב: ״וְהֵבִיא אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ לַה׳״, וּלְבַסּוֹף לִכְתּוֹב ״בִּקּוֹרֶת תִּהְיֶה״. אַמַּאי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא בְּרֵישָׁא: ״בִּקּוֹרֶת תִּהְיֶה״ וּלְבַסּוֹף כְּתַב: ״וְהֵבִיא אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ לַה׳״? הָכִי קָאָמַר: אִם בִּקּוֹרֶת תִּהְיֶה הִיא – ״וְהֵבִיא אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ לַה׳״, וְאִם לֹא תִּהְיֶה בִּקּוֹרֶת – לֹא יָבִיא הוּא אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ.

a7.he: אֵימָא, הוּא מַעֲטֵיהּ קְרָא, אֲבָל הִיא תִּילְקֵי וְתַיְתֵי קׇרְבָּן! – ״וְהֵבִיא אֶת אֲשָׁמוֹ לַה׳״ כְּתִיב.

a8.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל שִׁפְחָה בְּעוּלָה בִּלְבָד, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְהִיא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ״. וּמַאי מַשְׁמַע, דְּהַאי ״נֶחֱרֶפֶת״ לִישָּׁנָא דְּשַׁנּוֹיֵי הוּא? דִּכְתִיב ״וַתִּשְׁטַח עָלָיו הָרִיפוֹת״. וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: ״אִם תִּכְתּוֹשׁ הָאֱוִיל בַּמַּכְתֵּשׁ בְּתוֹךְ הָרִיפוֹת בַּעֱלִי״.

a9.he: ״וַיִּתְּנוּ יָדָם לְהוֹצִיא נְשֵׁיהֶם וַאֲשֵׁמִים אֵיל צֹאן עַל אַשְׁמָתָם״, אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכּוּלָּן שְׁפָחוֹת חֲרוּפוֹת בָּעֲלוּ.

a10.he: אֵיזוֹהִי שִׁפְחָה כּוּ׳. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְהׇפְדֵּה״, יָכוֹל כּוּלָּהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״לֹא נִפְדָּתָה״. יָכוֹל לֹא נִפְדָּתָה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהׇפְדֵּה״,

a11.he: הָא כֵיצַד? פְּדוּיָה וְאֵינָהּ פְּדוּיָה – חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָיהּ בַּת חוֹרִין וּמְאוֹרֶסֶת לְעֶבֶד עִבְרִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: בְּשִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, וּמְאוֹרֶסֶת לְעֶבֶד עִבְרִי. אִם כֵּן מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה״? דִּבְּרָה תוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם.

a12.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת מְפוֹרָשׁוֹת לָנוּ, מְשׁוּיָּיר לָנוּ חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין וּמְאוֹרֶסֶת לְעֶבֶד עִבְרִי. אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: ״לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי לֹא חוּפָּשָׁה״ – בְּשִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר, וּמְאוֹרֶסֶת לְעֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי.

a13.he: לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, בִּשְׁלָמָא ״וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה״ – כִּדְקָתָנֵי: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם, אֶלָּא דְּקָתָנֵי: מְאוֹרֶסֶת לְעֶבֶד עִבְרִי, מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי לֹא חוּפָּשָׁה״, מִכְּלָל דְּהוּא חוּפַּשׁ.

a14.he: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הַיְינוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא! לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל קָאָמַר: לְדִידִי, בְּעָלְמָא כְּווֹתָיךְ סְבִירָא לֵיהּ דְּדִבְּרָה תוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם, וְהָכָא שָׁאנֵי. מִכְּדֵי כְּתִיב לֵיהּ קְרָא: ״כִּי לֹא חוּפָּשָׁה״, ״וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה״ לְמָה לִי? שְׁמַע מִינָּה לְהָכִי אֲתָא, לְחֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין.

a15.he: לַאֲחֵרִים, בִּשְׁלָמָא ״וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה״, קָסָבַר: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם, אֶלָּא הָא דְּעֶבֶד כְּנַעֲנִי מְנָלַן? אֲמַר קְרָא: ״כִּי לֹא חוּפָּשָׁה״, אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לְדִידַהּ – תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן לְדִידֵיהּ.

a16.he: מַתְנִי׳ כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת, אֶחָד גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד קָטָן – קָטָן פָּטוּר, אֶחָד עֵר וְאֶחָד יָשֵׁן – יָשֵׁן פָּטוּר, אֶחָד שׁוֹגֵג וְאֶחָד מֵזִיד – שׁוֹגֵג בְּחַטָּאת וּמֵזִיד בְּהִכָּרֵת.

a17.he: גְּמָ׳ וְהָכָא, חַיָּיב קָטָן? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, הָכִי קָתָנֵי: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת, אֶחָד גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד קָטָן – קָטָן פָּטוּר וְגָדוֹל חַיָּיב, וְהָכָא – גָּדוֹל נָמֵי פָּטוּר, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּהָא מִקַּשְׁיָין אַהֲדָדֵי.

a18.he: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת, אֶחָד נֵיעוֹר וְאֶחָד יָשֵׁן – פָּטוּר. וְכָאן, יָשֵׁן נָמֵי חַיָּיב? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, הָכִי קָתָנֵי: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת, אֶחָד נֵיעוֹר וְאֶחָד יָשֵׁן – יָשֵׁן פָּטוּר וְנֵיעוֹר חַיָּיב, וְכָאן – אֲפִילּוּ נֵיעוֹר פָּטוּר, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּמִקַּשְׁיָין אַהֲדָדֵי.

a19.he: תָּנֵי תַּנָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת: עָשׂוּ גּוֹמֵר כִּמְעָרֶה, מִתְכַּוֵּין כְּשֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין, כְּדַרְכָּהּ כְּשֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ, נֵיעוֹר כְּיָשֵׁן.

a20.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי קָאָמְרַתְּ? אִי בְּשִׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה קָתָנֵי, אַמַּאי עָשׂוּ גּוֹמֵר כִּמְעָרֶה? גּוֹמֵר בְּשִׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה מִיחַיַּיב, מְעָרֶה לָא מִיחַיַּיב! וְתוּ: מִתְכַּוֵּין כְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִתְכַּוֵּין, אִי מִכַּוְּונָה – מִיחַיְּיבָא, אִי לָא – לָא מִיחַיְּיבָא!

a21.he: וּכְדַרְכָּהּ כְּשֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ נָמֵי, כְּדַרְכָּהּ בְּשִׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה מִיחַיַּיב, וְשֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ לָא מִיחַיַּיב, מַאי טַעְמָא? ״שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע״ כְּתִיב! וּמַאי נֵיעוֹר כְּיָשֵׁן?

a22.he: וְאִי בִּשְׁאָר עֲרָיוֹת קָא תָנֵי, עָשׂוּ גּוֹמֵר כִּמְעָרֶה?

b2.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיסְמְיַיהּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא, הָכִי קָתָנֵי: עָשׂוּ גּוֹמֵר שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ בְּשִׁפְחָה חֲרוּפָה, דְּלָא מִיחַיְּיבִי, כִּמְעָרֶה כְּדַרְכָּהּ, דְּ״שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע״ כְּתִיב.

b3.he: מִתְכַּוֵּין שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ בְּשִׁפְחָה, דִּפְטוּרִין כְּאֵינוֹ מִתְכַּוֵּין, דְּ״שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע״ כְּתִיב. נֵיעוֹר שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ בְּשִׁפְחָה, דִּפְטוּרִין כְּיָשֵׁן, מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּ״שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע״ כְּתִיב.

b4.he: נִמְצָא מִתְכַּוֵּין וְהַמְעָרֶה בְּשִׁפְחָה, כְּשֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין בְּכׇל עֲרָיוֹת. יָשֵׁן כְּדַרְכָּהּ – כְּיָשֵׁן דַּעֲרָיוֹת, נִמְצָא נֵיעוֹר שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ בְּשִׁפְחָה – כְּיָשֵׁן דְּכׇל עֲרָיוֹת.

b6.he: מַתְנִי׳ אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אָכַלְתָּ חֵלֶב – מֵבִיא חַטָּאת. עֵד אוֹמֵר: אָכַל, וְעֵד אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָכַל, אִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת: אָכַל, וְאִשָּׁה אוֹמֶרֶת: לֹא אָכַל – מֵבִיא אָשָׁם תָּלוּי. עֵד אוֹמֵר: אָכַל, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָכַלְתִּי – פָּטוּר.

b7.he: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים: אָכַל, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָכַלְתִּי – רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב. אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם הֱבִיאוּהוּ שְׁנַיִם לִידֵי מִיתָה חֲמוּרָה, לֹא יְבִיאוּהוּ לִידֵי קׇרְבָּן הַקַּל? אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מָה אִם יִרְצֶה לוֹמַר ״מֵזִיד הָיִיתִי״ – פָּטוּר.

b8.he: אָכַל חֵלֶב וְחֵלֶב בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת. אָכַל חֵלֶב וָדָם וּפִיגּוּל וְנוֹתָר בְּהֶעְלֵם (אַחַת) [אֶחָד] – חַיָּיב עַל כׇּל אַחַת וְאַחַת. זֶה חוֹמֶר בְּמִינִין הַרְבֵּה מִמִּין אֶחָד.

b9.he: וְחוֹמֶר בְּמִין אֶחָד מִמִּינִין הַרְבֵּה, שֶׁאִם אָכַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וְחָזַר וְאָכַל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת אַחֵר בְּהֶעְלֵם אֶחָד, מִמִּין אֶחָד – חַיָּיב, מִשְּׁנֵי מִינִין – פָּטוּר.

b10.he: גְּמָ׳ קָתָנֵי: אָמְרוּ לוֹ ״אָכַלְתָּ חֵלֶב״ – מֵבִיא חַטָּאת. אָמְרוּ כְּמָה הָוְיָין? תְּרֵין. וְהוּא מָה אָמַר לְהוֹן? אִלֵּימָא דְּשָׁתֵיק וְלָא קָמַכְחֵישׁ לְהוּ, אֶלָּא שְׁתִיקָה דִּתְרֵין הוּא דְּמֵבִיא חַטָּאת, עַל שְׁתִיקָה דְּחַד – לָא.

b11.he: אֵימָא מְצִיעֲתָא, עֵד אוֹמֵר: אָכַל, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: לֹא אָכַלְתִּי. טַעְמָא דְּמַכְחִישׁ לֵיהּ, אֲבָל שָׁתֵיק – מִיחַיַּיב, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן תְּרֵי!

b12.he: אֶלָּא: דְּקָמַכְחֵישׁ לְהוּ, מַנִּי – רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: הַכְחָשָׁה דְּבֵי תְרֵי לָאו הַכְחָשָׁה הִיא, אֲבָל לְרַבָּנַן, פָּטוּר.

b13.he: וּמַאי קָמַשְׁמַע לַן? מִסֵּיפָא שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ! הָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן: דָּבָר זֶה מַחְלוֹקֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבָּנַן, וְהוּא דְּקָמַכְחֵישׁ לְהוּ.

b14.he: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: ״אָמְרוּ לוֹ״ נָמֵי חַד קָרֵי לֵיהּ, דִּתְנַן: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלַךְ בַּעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם וּבָאוּ וְאָמְרוּ לָהּ מֵת בַּעֲלִיךְ וְנִישֵּׂאת וְאַחַר כָּךְ בָּא בַּעְלָהּ – תֵּצֵא מִזֶּה וּמִזֶּה, דְּקַיְימָא לַן דַּאֲפִילּוּ בְּחַד.

b15.he: מִמַּאי? מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: נִישֵּׂאת שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת – מוּתֶּרֶת לַחְזוֹר לוֹ. מַאי שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת – שֶׁלֹּא בִּרְשׁוּת בֵּית דִּין וְעֵד אֶחָד,

b16.he: מִכְּלָל דְּרֵישָׁא, בִּרְשׁוּת בֵּית דִּין וּבְעֵד אֶחָד. אַלְמָא גַּבֵּי עֵד אֶחָד קָתָנֵי ״אָמְרוּ״, וְהָכָא נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי ״אָמְרוּ לוֹ״, מַשְׁמַע אֲפִילּוּ עֵד אֶחָד.

b17.he: וְהוּא, מַאי קָאָמַר? אִלֵּימָא דְּקָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ, מִי מַיְיתֵי? וְהָא קָתָנֵי מְצִיעֲתָא: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: אָכַל, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר לֹא אָכַלְתִּי – פָּטוּר!

b18.he: אֶלָּא דְּשָׁתֵיק, מִמְּצִיעֲתָא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: עֵד אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: כּוּ׳. טַעְמָא דְּקָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ, אֲבָל שָׁתֵק מִישְׁתָּק – חַיָּיב!

b19.he: לְעוֹלָם דְּלָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אָכַלְתָּ חֵלֶב – מֵבִיא חַטָּאת. בַּמֶּה דְבָרִים אֲמוּרִים: דְּשָׁתֵיק, אֲבָל מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ – פָּטוּר.

b20.he: וּמִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מְנָלַן דְּלָא מַכְחֵישׁ לֵיהּ חַיָּיב? דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו חַטָּאתוֹ״ – וְלֹא שֶׁיּוֹדִיעוּהוּ אֲחֵרִים. יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ אֵין מַכְחִישָׁן? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו״ – מִכׇּל מָקוֹם.

b21.he: בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִלֵּימָא בִּתְרֵין, תְּרֵין וְאֵין מַכְחִישָׁן קְרָא בָּעֵי?

messages.text: Continued from 10b: the mishna lists how an espoused maidservant differs from all others with whom relations are forbidden: a guilt offering rather than a sin offering, a male animal rather than a female, lashes for her alone and an offering for him alone, and liability only for completing the act. It ends: This is a stringency that the Torah imposed with regard to the maidservant:
Mishna

That the Torah established her status so that the one who engages in intercourse with her intentionally is like the one who does so unwittingly, as both are liable to bring a guilt offering, whereas one who engages in intercourse with those with whom relations are forbidden is liable to bring a sin offering only when he does so unwittingly.

Who is the espoused maidservant in question? It is any woman who is half-maidservant half-free woman, i.e., a maidservant who belonged to two masters, one of whom liberated her, as it is stated: “And she was redeemed and not redeemed” (Leviticus 19:20), which means that she was partially but not completely redeemed. This is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed.

messages.text: An espoused maidservant is a full-fledged maidservant whose status is certain, as the language of the verse does not mean redeemed and not redeemed; it is simply a way of stating that she was not redeemed.

notes.he: גמורה:
notes.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: a maidservant: a full-fledged one.

notes.he: זו היא שפחה ודאי שאינה פדויה כלל:
notes.en: Rabbi Yishmael says: This is a certain maidservant: who is not redeemed at all.

messages.text: All those with whom relations are forbidden are enumerated in the Torah, and we have no exception other than one who is half-maidservant half-free woman.

notes.he: שהן בנות חורין ושיור אין לנו וזו ודאי משונה היא חציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין:
notes.en: All those with whom relations are forbidden are enumerated: [all of them] are free women, and we have no exception; and this one is certainly different: she is half-maidservant and half-free woman.

messages.text: Gemara
The mishna teaches that in the case of an espoused maidservant the Torah did not equate the man with the woman. From where do we derive that she is flogged and that he is not flogged?

The verse states: “And if a man lies carnally with a woman, and she is a maidservant designated for a man…there shall be an inspection [bikkoret tihye]” (Leviticus 19:20). This teaches that she is flogged.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed.

messages.text: And as one might have thought that both are flogged, the verse states: “There shall be [tihye],” in the feminine, to teach that she is flogged and he is not flogged.
And from where is it derived that this word inspection [bikkoret] is a term for flogging?
It indicates that she shall be subjected to the reciting of [bikra’ei] the verses,

notes.he: שהן קורין עליה והפלא ה' את מכותך שכן קורין על הלוקין במס' מכות (דף כב:):
notes.en: Gemara. She shall be [subjected] to the reciting: for they recite over her: “Then the Lord will make your plagues extraordinary” (Deuteronomy 28:59), as they recite over those who are flogged, in tractate Makkot (22b).

notes.he: תימה הלא לא מפרש שצריך לקרות בשעה שמלקין אם לא מכאן:
notes.en: She shall be [subjected] to the readings: This is puzzling: for [nowhere] is it explained that one must recite at the time that one flogs, if not from here.

notes.he: תהא בקראי בהקראה כדתנן גדול שבדיינין מקרא בשעת מלקות אם לא תשמור לעשות והפלא ה' את מכותך:
notes.en: [An editor’s marker notes that what precedes belongs to 10b.] She shall be [subjected] to the readings: to the reciting, as we learned: The greatest of the judges recites at the time of the flogging: “If you will not observe to do… then the Lord will make your plagues extraordinary” (Deuteronomy 28:58–59).

messages.text: The procedure for administering lashes is that before each lash is administered, the eldest or most prominent of the three judges recites the relevant verses in the Torah; the second-eldest one counts the lashes; and the third says to the attendant: Strike him.
It indicates that she shall be subject to an assessment [bikkur],

notes.he: שאם אינה יכולה לקבל ארבעים אומדין אותה בבקור ובמחשבה:
notes.en: She shall be subject to an assessment: for if she cannot withstand forty [lashes], they assess her by examination and reckoning.

notes.he: באומד היינו מלקות כדתנן אין אומדין אותו כו':
notes.en: She shall be subject to an assessment: by estimate; that is flogging, as we learned: One assesses him only, etc.

messages.text: One assesses the number of lashes that the one sentenced to be flogged is capable of withstanding, but only by a number of lashes fit to be divided by three.

notes.he: כגון י"ח או כ"א או כ"ד שהיו מכין אותו שתי ידות (מלפניו ואחת מאחריו) ומקרא ילפינן לה במס' מכות (דף כג.):
notes.en: Lashes fit to be divided by three: for example eighteen, or twenty-one, or twenty-four, for they would strike him two parts (in front of him and one behind him) [so the text reads; the mishna in Makkot 22b has one third in front and two thirds behind], and we derive it from a verse in tractate Makkot (23a).

messages.text: This teaches that the assessment is an essential part of the flogging procedure.
At the time that, i.e., in any case where, the woman is flogged, the man brings an offering. In a case where the woman is not flogged, the man does not bring an offering.

notes.he: שגדולה היא ובת עונשין היא:
notes.en: At the time that the woman is flogged: that she is an adult and subject to punishment.

notes.he: כגון שהיא שוגגת וקטנה אין האיש מביא קרבן והא דאמרינן לרבות שוגג כמזיד היינו שוגג דאיש כמזיד אבל האשה צריך שתהא מזידה:
notes.en: The woman is not flogged: for example, where she acted unwittingly or is a minor, the man does not bring an offering. And as for what we say, “to include the unwitting like the intentional,” that means the man’s unwitting [act] is like [his] intentional one; but the woman must have acted intentionally.

notes.he: שהיא גדולה והוא גדול האיש מביא קרבן:
notes.en: At the time that the woman is flogged: where she is an adult and he is an adult, the man brings an offering.

notes.he: שהיא קטנה אין האיש מביא קרבן אע"פ שהוא גדול:
notes.en: The woman is not flogged: where she is a minor, the man does not bring an offering, even though he is an adult.

messages.text: From where do we derive this?
messages.quote: the woman is flogged, the man brings an offering

messages.text: It is as it is written: “And if a man lies carnally with a woman, and she is a maidservant designated for a man, and not at all redeemed, nor was freedom given her; there shall be an inspection…He shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord” (Leviticus 19:20–21).

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃ וְהֵבִיא אֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ לַיהֹוָה אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֵיל אָשָׁם׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed. But he must bring to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, as his reparation offering to GOD, a ram of reparation offering.

messages.text: Since until here, the verse is dealing with a man, let it first write: “He shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord,” and at the end let it write: “There shall be an inspection.” Why did the Merciful One first write: “There shall be an inspection,” and at the end write: “He shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord”?

notes.he: או חופשה לא ניתן לה באיש קא משתעי אשר ישכב את אשה שכבת זרע נכתוב ברישא כו':
notes.en: Since until here: [up to] “nor was freedom given her,” the verse speaks about the man: “A man who lies carnally with a woman”; let it write first, etc.

messages.text: This is what the verse is saying: If there will be an inspection, meaning that the woman is to be flogged, then “he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord.” But if there will not be an inspection, then he shall not bring his guilt offering.

notes.he: שהיא גדולה וכדרכה ומתכונת:
notes.en: This is what it is saying: If there will be an inspection: that she is an adult, [the act was] in the typical manner, and she intended.

notes.he: והביא הוא את אשמו כשהיא בביקורת:
notes.en: He shall bring his guilt offering: when she is [subject] to the inspection.

messages.text: You can say that the verse in fact excludes him from being flogged due to the use of the term “there shall be,” thereby limiting his liability to bring a guilt offering; but even so, she should be flogged and also bring an offering.

notes.he: מהדר אמתני' דקתני לא השוה אשה לאיש לקרבן אימא הוא מיעטיה קרא ממלקות דכתיב תהיה אבל היא אימא תילקי ותייתי קרבן:
notes.en: Say that the verse excludes him: [the Gemara] goes back to the mishna, which teaches that [the Torah] did not equate the woman with the man with regard to an offering. Say that the verse excludes him from lashes, as it is written “there shall be” [in the feminine]; but as for her, say that she is flogged and brings an offering.

notes.he: לא לקי דמעטיה קרא בקורת תהיה היא ולא הוא:
notes.en: And say that he: is not flogged, for the verse excluded him: “There shall be an inspection,” she and not he.

messages.text: “He shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord,” is written in the verse, instead of merely: He shall bring a guilt offering. This teaches that only he, and not she, brings a guilt offering.

notes.he: ולא והביאה את אשמה:
notes.en: “He shall bring his guilt offering” is written: and not “she shall bring her guilt offering.”

messages.text: Actually, he is liable only in a case where he engages in intercourse with a non-virgin maidservant, as it is stated: “And she is a maidservant designated [neḥerefet] for a man.”

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed.

notes.dh: לעולם אינו חייב קרבן אלא על שפחה בעולה
notes.he: שנתבעלה קודם לכן:
notes.en: Actually, he is liable to an offering only for a non-virgin maidservant: who had intercourse before that.

messages.text: And from where may it be inferred that this word “designated [neḥerefet],” is a term of change, i.e., that she has already changed from her status as a virgin to that of a non-virgin?

notes.he: שנשתנית מברייתה:
notes.en: It is a term of change: that she has changed from her natural state.

messages.text: As it is written: “And strewed groats [harifot] thereon” (II Samuel 17:19). Since groats are grains that have been crushed or otherwise changed from their original form, the linguistic correlation between harifot and neḥerefet indicates that both terms are referring to some form of change.

verse.he: וַתִּקַּח הָאִשָּׁה וַתִּפְרֹשׂ אֶת־הַמָּסָךְ עַל־פְּנֵי הַבְּאֵר וַתִּשְׁטַח עָלָיו הָרִפוֹת וְלֹא נוֹדַע דָּבָר׃
verse.en: and the wife took a cloth, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered groats on top of it, so that nothing would be noticed.

notes.he: דבר שנשתנה ע"י כתישה וכאן נמי ע"י אבר שמש דש:
notes.en: Groats [harifot]: something that has changed through pounding; and here too [she has changed] through the male organ in intercourse.

notes.he: חרופה כגון הריפות שנשתנו מתחלתן:
notes.en: Designated [ḥarufa]: like groats [harifot], which have changed from their original [state].

messages.text: And if you wish, say that it is inferred from the verse: “Though you should bray a fool in a mortar with a pestle among groats [harifot]” (Proverbs 27:22).

verse.he: אִם־תִּכְתּוֹשׁ־אֶת־הָאֱוִיל ׀ בַּמַּכְתֵּשׁ בְּתוֹךְ הָרִיפוֹת בַּעֱלִי לֹא־תָסוּר מֵעָלָיו אִוַּלְתּוֹ׃ {פ}
verse.en:
Even if you pound the fool in a mortar
With a pestle along with grain,
His folly will not leave him.

notes.he: שכבר נכתשת היא על ידי בעילה ונשתנית כהריפות:
notes.en: Though you should bray: for she has already been pounded through intercourse and changed, like groats.

messages.text: It is stated in another verse: “And among the sons of the priests there were found some that had married foreign women, namely: Of the sons of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and his brethren, Maaseiah, and Eliezer, and Jarib, and Gedaliah. And they gave their hand that they would divorce their wives; and being guilty, a ram of the flock for their guilt” (Ezra 10:18–19).

verse.he: וַיִּמָּצֵא מִבְּנֵי הַכֹּהֲנִים אֲשֶׁר הֹשִׁיבוּ נָשִׁים נׇכְרִיּוֹת מִבְּנֵי יֵשׁוּעַ בֶּן־יוֹצָדָק וְאֶחָיו מַעֲשֵׂיָה וֶאֱלִיעֶזֶר וְיָרִיב וּגְדַלְיָה׃ וַיִּתְּנוּ יָדָם לְהוֹצִיא נְשֵׁיהֶם וַאֲשֵׁמִים אֵיל־צֹאן עַל־אַשְׁמָתָם׃ {ס}
verse.en: Among the priestly families who were found to have brought foreign women were Jeshua son of Jozadak and his brothers Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah. They gave their word to expel their wives and, acknowledging their guilt, offered a ram from the flock to expiate it.

notes.he: פסוק הוא בספר עזרא:
notes.en: And they gave their hand that they would divorce: it is a verse in the book of Ezra.

notes.he: נכריות בימי עזרא:
notes.en: To divorce their wives: the foreign women, in the days of Ezra.

messages.text: This teaches that they had all engaged in intercourse with espoused maidservants, as guilt offerings are brought for engaging in intercourse only with an espoused maidservant.

notes.he: שפחות חרופות בעלו דחייבין עליה איל אשם:
notes.en: They had intercourse with espoused maidservants: for which one is liable to a ram as a guilt offering.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches: Which is the espoused maidservant? According to Rabbi Yehuda, it is any woman who is half-maidservant and half-free woman, whereas Rabbi Yishmael maintains that it is referring to a full-fledged maidservant.
messages.quote: Who is the espoused maidservant in question?

messages.text: “And she was redeemed” (Leviticus 19:20): One might have thought that this means she was entirely redeemed. Therefore, the verse states: “And she was redeemed and not redeemed,” to teach that she was not entirely redeemed.
messages.lead: In relation to this dispute, the Sages taught in a baraita that deals with the verse:

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed.

notes.he: אי לא נפדתה יכול כולה לא נפדתה כלל ת"ל והפדה:
notes.en: If “not redeemed,” I might think that she was not redeemed at all; the verse states: “And she was redeemed.”

messages.text: If so, one might have thought that she was not redeemed at all. Therefore, the verse states: “And she was redeemed,” to teach that it is discussing a maidservant who was partially redeemed.
How so?

The verse is referring to a maidservant who was both redeemed and not redeemed, as half of her is a maidservant owned by one master who did not redeem her, and half of her is a free woman, as the partner who previously owned the other half of her has freed her, and she is betrothed to a Hebrew slave. This is the statement of Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: והפדה לא נפדתה משמע פדויה ואינה פדויה:
notes.en: Redeemed [and not redeemed]: “and not at all redeemed” [vehofdeh lo nifdata] implies redeemed and not redeemed.

notes.he: דכתיב נחרפת לאיש דחרופה נמי היינו לשון קדושין כדאמר במסכת קידושין חרופתי. (ידיעתי) מאורסת לישראל ליכא למימר דכיון דחציה שפחה אסורה לבן ישראל אבל עבד עברי מותר בין בשפחה כנענית בין בישראלית:
notes.en: And betrothed to a Hebrew slave: for it is written: “Designated [neḥerefet] for a man,” and ḥarufa is also a term of betrothal, as it says in tractate Kiddushin [an editor suggests reading: one who says “my ḥarufa,” she is betrothed]: “my ḥarufa” ([a variant:] “my designated”). [That she is] betrothed to a Jew cannot be said, for since she is half-maidservant she is forbidden to a Jew; but a Hebrew slave is permitted both to a Canaanite maidservant and to a Jewish woman.

messages.text: The verse is speaking of a Canaanite maidservant who was not redeemed at all and who is engaged to a Hebrew slave. If so, why must the verse state: “And she was redeemed and not redeemed”? The repetition is not halakhically significant; it is there because the Torah spoke in the language of people, and the phrase simply means: And she was not at all redeemed.

notes.he: דלא נפדתה כלל:
notes.en: The Torah spoke in the language of people: [meaning] that she was not redeemed at all.

messages.text: All those with whom relations are forbidden are enumerated for us explicitly in the Torah. The only case which is excluded for us from that generalization is a half-maidservant half-free woman who is betrothed to a Hebrew slave.

notes.he: בתורה היאך חיובן משוייר אין לנו שלא נתפרש בתורה אלא זו בלבד שבחציה שפחה וחציה בת חורין חייב ולא באחרת וראב"ע היינו ר' עקיבא (קא בעי) [כדאמר] בגמרא לקמן:
notes.en: All those with whom relations are forbidden are enumerated: in the Torah, how one is liable for them. We have no exception that was not made explicit in the Torah except this alone: that for one who is half-maidservant and half-free woman one is liable, and not for another [maidservant]. And Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya is [the same as] Rabbi Akiva, as is said in the Gemara below.

messages.text: When it states: “They shall not be put to death because she was not free,” the verse is speaking about a Canaanite maidservant who is betrothed to a Canaanite slave.

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed.

notes.he: לאו דוקא דהא לא תפסו בה קדושין:
notes.en: Betrothed to a Canaanite slave: not precisely, for betrothal does not take effect with her.

messages.text: According to Rabbi Yishmael, granted that the phrase “and she was redeemed and not redeemed” is referring simply to a Canaanite maidservant, as it is taught in the baraita: The Torah spoke in the language of people. But from where do we derive that which is taught, i.e., that she is betrothed specifically to a Hebrew slave?
messages.quote: is engaged to a Hebrew slave

notes.dh: לרבי ישמעאל מאורסת לעבד עברי מנא ליה
notes.he: בשלמא לר"ע דמוקי לה בחציה בת חורין לא בעיא קרא דאיכא למימר מדחייב עלה רחמנא ודאי מאורסת היא מישראל דהא תפסו לה קדושין הילכך איכא למימר לעבד עברי נתקדשה שהרי רבו מוסרה לו בעל כרחו כדמפרש בקדושין (דף יד:) ולא לעבד כנעני שהרי אסורה לו אלא לרבי ישמעאל דאמר שפחה גמורה מאורסת לעבד עברי מנא ליה (דאמר לעבד עברי שהרי אסורה לו) דילמא לעבד כנעני דהא לדידיה שריא לגמרי טפי מעברי:
notes.en: According to Rabbi Yishmael, from where does he derive betrothed to a Hebrew slave: Granted, according to Rabbi Akiva, who establishes [the verse] as one who is half free, no verse is needed, for one can say: since the Merciful One rendered [the man] liable for her, she is certainly betrothed to a Jew, as betrothal takes effect with her. Therefore one can say that she was betrothed to a Hebrew slave, for his master gives her to him even against his will, as is explained in Kiddushin (14b), and not to a Canaanite slave, for she is forbidden to him. But according to Rabbi Yishmael, who says she is a full-fledged maidservant, from where does he derive [that she is] betrothed to a Hebrew slave? (The printed text adds here, in parentheses: “that he says to a Hebrew slave, since she is forbidden to him.”) Perhaps [she is betrothed] to a Canaanite slave, since according to him she is entirely permitted [to a Canaanite slave], more so than to a Hebrew one.

notes.dh: ורבי ישמעאל בשלמא והפדה כו' דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם
notes.he: והכי נמי קאמר בירושלמי לשונות כפולים הן והתורה דברה בהן הלך הלכת נכסוף נכספת גנב גנבתי ור"ע פליג ובכל דוכתא דקאמר הניחא למ"ד דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם אלא למ"ד וכו' היינו ר' ישמעאל ור"ע:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Yishmael, granted “and not at all redeemed,” etc., the Torah spoke in the language of people: And so too it says in the Jerusalem Talmud: they are doubled expressions, and the Torah spoke with them: “you have gone, you have gone [halokh halakhta],” “you longed, you longed [nikhsof nikhsafta],” “I was indeed stolen [gunov gunavti]”; and Rabbi Akiva disagrees. And everywhere that it says: “This works out well according to the one who says the Torah spoke in the language of people, but according to the one who says, etc.,” that is Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva.

notes.he: בשלמא לר' עקיבא לא איצטריך למימר דלא קמ"ל רבותא דכיון דחציה בת חורין ראויה לינשא לעבד עברי אלא לר' ישמעאל לעבד עברי אמאי דכתיב כי לא חופשה מכלל דהוא חופש. דאינו כנעני אלא עברי:
notes.en: Granted according to Rabbi Yishmael, etc.: Granted according to Rabbi Akiva, it is not necessary [an editor suggests reading: a verse is not necessary for this, for necessarily it speaks of a Hebrew slave, since being half free she is fit to marry only a Hebrew slave] to say it, for it does not teach us a novelty, since being half free she is fit to marry a Hebrew slave. But according to Rabbi Yishmael, why a Hebrew slave? Because it is written: “Because she was not free”; by inference, he is free: he is not Canaanite but Hebrew.

messages.text: It is as it is written: “They shall not be put to death, because she was not free” (Leviticus 19:20). By inference, it may be concluded that he, the man to whom she is betrothed, is free. A Hebrew slave is not the property of his owner, but is merely obligated to serve him for a period of time.
The opinion of Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya is identical to the opinion of Rabbi Akiva. Why was it stated separately in the baraita?
messages.quote: half-maidservant half-free woman who is betrothed to a Hebrew slave

messages.text: According to me, in general I hold in accordance with your opinion, that the Torah spoke in the language of people. But here it is different, since it is also written in the verse: “Because she was not free.” If so, why do I need the phrase “and she is redeemed and not redeemed”? Conclude from it that it comes for this purpose, to teach that the verse is referring to a woman who is half-maidservant half-free woman.
messages.lead: The Gemara explains: It is because Rabbi Elazar is saying to Rabbi Yishmael:

notes.dh: בעלמא כותך סבירא לי דדברה תורה כלשון בני אדם
notes.he: כדאמרינן הכרת תכרת ר' אלעזר אמר דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם והכא שאני דמכדי כו':
notes.en: In general I hold in accordance with you, that the Torah spoke in the language of people: as we say [about] “shall utterly be cut off [hikkaret tikkaret]”: Rabbi Elazar said: The Torah spoke in the language of people. And here it is different, for since, etc.

messages.text: According to Aḥerim, granted that the phrase “and she was redeemed and not redeemed” is referring to a Canaanite maidservant, as they too maintain that the Torah spoke in the language of people. But from where do we derive that she is betrothed to a Canaanite slave?
messages.quote: a Canaanite maidservant who is betrothed to a Canaanite slave

messages.text: The verse states: “Because she was not free,” and if it is not needed for the matter of her status as a maidservant, as it is already established that she is not free, apply it to the matter of his status as a slave.

notes.he: דהא כתיב (ויקרא יט) והפדה לא נפדתה:
notes.en: If it is not needed for the matter of her: for it is [already] written: “And not at all redeemed” (Leviticus 19:20).

notes.he: אם אינו ענין לדידה האי כי לא חופשה דהא כתיב והפדה לא נפדתה תנהו ענין לדידיה דאינו חופש דהיינו כנעני הוא:
notes.en: If it is not needed for the matter of her: this “because she was not free,” for it is [already] written: “And not at all redeemed,” apply it to the matter of him: that he is not free, that is, he is Canaanite.

messages.text: Mishna
In all cases of intercourse with those with whom relations are forbidden, if one is an adult and one is a minor, the minor is exempt;
messages.lead: This mishna cites an additional difference between the status of an espoused maidservant and the status of forbidden relatives.

notes.he: אם האחד גדול או האיש או האשה האחד חייב והאחד פטור ובשפחה אינו כן ובגמרא מפרש לה:
notes.en: Mishna. All those with whom relations are forbidden: if one of them is an adult, whether the man or the woman, the one is liable and the other exempt; and with the maidservant it is not so, and the Gemara explains it.

notes.he: או הזכר או הנקבה:
notes.en: One is an adult and one is a minor: either the male or the female.

messages.text: if one is awake and one is sleeping, the sleeping one is exempt;

if one commits the act unwittingly and one does so intentionally, the one who did so unwittingly is liable to bring a sin offering and the one who did so intentionally is liable to be punished with karet. By contrast, in a case of intercourse with an espoused maidservant, the man is liable to bring a guilt offering only if the woman is flogged, and that is the case only if she was an adult, awake, and committed the sin intentionally.

notes.he: ובשפחה נהי דאם הוא מזיד והיא שוגגת דפטורין הואיל ואינה לוקה כדאמרינן לעיל בקורת תהיה והביא את אשמו ואי לא פטורין מיהו אם הוא שוגג והיא מזידה היא במלקות והוא באשם כדאמרי' בהאי פירקא דשוגג ומזיד שוין בבא על השפחה:
notes.en: Unwitting with a sin offering and intentional with karet: and with the maidservant, granted that if he acted intentionally and she unwittingly they are exempt, since she is not flogged, as we said above: “There shall be an inspection… and he shall bring his guilt offering,” and if not, they are exempt. But if he acted unwittingly and she intentionally, she is [liable] to lashes and he to a guilt offering, as we say in this chapter that the unwitting and the intentional are equal for one who has intercourse with the maidservant.

messages.text: Gemara
And is that to say that here, in the case of an espoused maidservant, a minor is liable? But a minor is exempt from all liabilities in the Torah.

notes.he: בתמיה וכי קטן חייב בשפחה:
notes.en: Gemara. And here a minor is liable: asked in astonishment: is a minor liable with the maidservant?

notes.he: והבא על שפחה חרופה קטן חייב בתמיהא אמאי:
notes.en: A minor is exempt: and for one who has intercourse with an espoused maidservant, is a minor liable? Asked in astonishment: why [would he be]?

messages.text: This is what the mishna is teaching: In all cases of intercourse with those with whom relations are forbidden, if one is an adult and one is a minor, the minor is exempt and the adult is liable. But here, in the case of an espoused maidservant, the adult is also exempt.

What is the reason? Their punishments are linked, as they are juxtaposed to each other in the verse: “There shall be an inspection…and he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord” (Leviticus 19:20–21).

verse.he: וְאִישׁ כִּי־יִשְׁכַּב אֶת־אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת־זֶרַע וְהִוא שִׁפְחָה נֶחֱרֶפֶת לְאִישׁ וְהׇפְדֵּה לֹא נִפְדָּתָה אוֹ חֻפְשָׁהֿ לֹא נִתַּן־לָהּ בִּקֹּרֶת תִּהְיֶה לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי־לֹא חֻפָּשָׁה׃ וְהֵבִיא אֶת־אֲשָׁמוֹ לַיהֹוָה אֶל־פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֵיל אָשָׁם׃
verse.en: If a man has carnal relations with a woman who is a slave and has been designated for another man, but has not been redeemed or given her freedom, there shall be an indemnity; they shall not, however, be put to death, since she has not been freed. But he must bring to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, as his reparation offering to GOD, a ram of reparation offering.

notes.he: כדאמרן לעיל אם אין האשה לוקה אין האיש מביא אשם:
notes.en: For they are juxtaposed to each other: as we said above: if the woman is not flogged, the man does not bring a guilt offering.

notes.he: הלשון אינו מכוון דהאיש הוקשה לאשה ולא אשה לאיש דהא כי האיש כמו האשה חייבת כדאיתא בת"כ ואיש פרט לקטן יכול שאני מוציא בן תשע שנים ויום אחד ת"ל ואיש א"כ אשה לא איתקשה לאיש:
notes.en: For they are juxtaposed to each other: The wording is not precise, for the man is juxtaposed to the woman, but the woman is not juxtaposed to the man; for [even] when the man [is a minor], the woman is liable, as is stated in the Torat Kohanim: “And a man” excludes a minor. Might I think that I exclude [even] a boy of nine years and one day? The verse states: “And a man.” If so, the woman is not juxtaposed to the man.

notes.he: וכאן בשפחה חרופה גדול נמי פטור כשהיא קטנה מ"ט דהא מיקשינן להדדי כדאמרי' לעיל אם בביקורת תהיה היא והביא הוא את אשמו:
notes.en: And here, with an espoused maidservant, the adult is also exempt when she is a minor. What is the reason? For they are juxtaposed to each other, as we said above: “If there will be an inspection,” she; “and he shall bring his guilt offering,” he.

messages.text: The mishna teaches: In all cases of intercourse with those with whom relations are forbidden, if one is awake and one is sleeping, the one who is sleeping is exempt. And is that to say that here the one who is sleeping is liable?

notes.he: בתמיה:
notes.en: And is one who is sleeping liable: asked in astonishment.

messages.text: This is what the mishna is teaching: In all cases of intercourse with those with whom relations are forbidden, if one is awake and one is sleeping, the one who is sleeping is exempt and the one who is awake is liable. But here, even the one who is awake is exempt.

What is the reason? Their punishments are linked, as they are juxtaposed to each other in the verse: “There shall be an inspection…and he shall bring his guilt offering unto the Lord” (Leviticus 19:20–21).

The Sages rendered one who completes the act of intercourse like one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse; one who commits the act intentionally like one who does so unintentionally; one who engages in intercourse in a typical manner like one who engages in intercourse in an atypical manner, i.e., anal intercourse; and one who is awake like one who is sleeping.

notes.he: פירש הקונט' משום דש"ז כתיב ובאין מתכוין אינו ראוי להזריע כגון נפל מן הגג ונתקע וקשה מאן לימא לן דאינו ראוי להזריע אלא האי טעמא משום שאנוס הוא:
notes.en: With one who does not intend (typical), he is exempt: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: because “lies carnally [shikhvat zera]” is written, and one who does not intend is not fit to inseminate, for example one who fell from a roof and was thrust in. But this is difficult: who tells us that he is not fit to inseminate? Rather, the reason is that he is a victim of circumstance [anus].

messages.text: What are you saying? If you are teaching this with regard to an espoused maidservant, why would you say that they rendered one who completes the act like one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse? This is not the case, as one who completes the act with an espoused maidservant is liable, but one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse is not liable.
messages.quote: rendered one who completes the act of intercourse like one who engages in the initial stage

notes.he: דשכבת זרע כתיב בה:
notes.en: One who engages in the initial stage is not liable: for “lies carnally [shikhvat zera]” is written with regard to her.

notes.he: דאיכא שכבת זרע בגמר ביאה:
notes.en: One who completes with a maidservant is liable: for there is “lying carnally [shikhvat zera]” at the completion of intercourse.

messages.text: And furthermore, they did not make one who commits the act intentionally like one who does so unintentionally: If she intended it, she is liable to receive lashes; if she did not intend it, she is not liable.

notes.dh: וכי מכוין מיחייב ואי לא לא מיחייב
notes.he: דשכבת זרע בעינן ושאינו מתכוין כגון נפל מן הגג ונתקע אין ראוי להזריע:
notes.en: If she intended it, she is liable, and if not, she is not liable: for we require “lies carnally [shikhvat zera],” and one who does not intend, for example one who fell from a roof and was thrust in, is not fit to inseminate.

notes.he: קא מיכוונא (היא) מיחייב בין היא ובין הוא:
notes.en: [If] she intends, [they are] liable: both she and he.

messages.text: And they also did not render engaging in intercourse in a typical manner like doing so in an atypical manner: One who engages in intercourse in a typical manner with an espoused maidservant is liable, and one who does so in an atypical manner is not liable. What is the reason? It is written: “Lies carnally [shikhvat zera],” and the literal meaning of this term is referring to intercourse that can lead to procreation, as zera means seed.

notes.he: והיא אינה מזרעת אלא בכדרכה:
notes.en: What is the reason? “Lies carnally [shikhvat zera]” is written: and she does not conceive except through typical [intercourse].

messages.text: And finally, in what way can it be said that they rendered one who is awake like one who is sleeping? One who is sleeping is always exempt, as the circumstances are beyond his control. Consequently, it seems that the baraita cannot be referring to intercourse with an espoused maidservant.

notes.dh: ותו אי בשפחה קא תנית ניעור כישן מאי ניהו לאו היינו ניהו מתכוין כשאין מתכוין
notes.he: דניעור מתכוין וישן אינו מתכוין:
notes.en: And furthermore, if you teach it with regard to a maidservant, awake like sleeping, what is that? Is it not the same as intending like not intending? For one who is awake intends, and one who is sleeping does not intend.

messages.text: And if you teach this baraita in relation to intercourse with all those others with whom relations are forbidden, how is it that they rendered one who completes the act like one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse?

notes.dh: ואי בשאר עריות קתני איפכא מיבעי ליה
notes.he: עשו מערה בעריות חייב כגומר שלא כדרכה חייב כבכדרכה דמשכבי אשה כתיב (ויקרא יט):
notes.en: And if he teaches it with regard to the other forbidden relations, it should teach the opposite: [that] they rendered one who engages in the initial stage with forbidden relations liable like one who completes, [and] atypical [intercourse] liable like typical, for “the lyings of a woman” [mishkevei isha] is written (Leviticus 19 [as printed]).

messages.text: It should teach the opposite, i.e., it should say: They made one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse like one who completes the act, as it is obvious that one who completes the act is liable.
Should I remove this baraita, as it is apparently corrupted?

notes.he: להא ברייתא הואיל וליכא לתרוצה:
notes.en: [An editor’s marker notes that what precedes belongs to 11a.] Should I remove it: this baraita, since there is no way to resolve it?

messages.text: No; do not remove the baraita, as this is what it is teaching: The Sages rendered one who completes an atypical act of intercourse with an espoused maidservant, for which he is not liable, like one who engages in the initial stage of intercourse with her in the typical manner, for which he is also exempt. They derived this from the fact that it is written: “Lies carnally.”

notes.he: והכי פירוש דברייתא עשו גומר כמערה ומתכוון כשאינו מתכוון והאי דינא הוי בכדרכה ושלא כדרכה כדמפרש הש"ס ומכל מקום קצת קשה אמאי לא תנא ניעור כישן בהדייהו ותנא ליה בתריה דכדרכה ושלא כדרכה:
notes.en: This is what it is teaching: they rendered, etc.: And this is the explanation of the baraita: they rendered one who completes like one who engages in the initial stage, and one who intends like one who does not intend, and this law is with typical and atypical [intercourse], as the Gemara explains. In any case it is slightly difficult: why did it not teach awake like sleeping together with them, but taught it after typical and atypical?

notes.he: עשו גומר בשלא כדרכה בשפחה כו':
notes.en: They rendered one who completes atypical [intercourse] with a maidservant, etc.

messages.text: Similarly, they rendered one who engages intentionally in atypical intercourse with a maidservant, for which they are both exempt, like one who does so in a typical manner unintentionally, as it is written: “Lies carnally.”

And they also rendered one who engages in intercourse in an atypical manner with an espoused maidservant while he is awake, for which they are both exempt, like one who does so while sleeping. What is the reason? They derived this from the fact that it is written: “Lies carnally.”

notes.dh: כשאין מתכוין בכדרכה דפטורה כגון שנפל מן הגג ונתקע
notes.he: והשתא קא בעי לתרוצה לדמוייה נמי לעריות לפטורה. נמצא מתכוין ומערה בשפחה בכוונה אפילו בכדרכה דפטור כשאין מתכוין בעריות דפטור והיינו עשו מתכוין כשאינו מתכוין דקאמר והכי נמי אין מתכוין כדרכה בשפחה פטור ישן כדרכה בשפחה פטור כישן דעריות דפטור כדתנן כל העריות אחד ניעור ואחד ישן ישן פטור:
notes.en: Like one who does not intend, in the typical manner, where she is exempt: for example, where he fell from a roof and was thrust in. And now [the Gemara] seeks to resolve it so as to compare it also to forbidden relations, [where one is] exempt. It is found that one who intends and engages in the initial stage with the maidservant intentionally, even in the typical manner, is exempt, like one who does not intend with forbidden relations, who is exempt; and that is [the meaning of] “they rendered one who intends like one who does not intend.” And likewise, one who does not intend, in the typical manner, with a maidservant is exempt; one sleeping, in the typical manner, with a maidservant is exempt, like one sleeping with forbidden relations, who is exempt, as we learned: [In] all [cases of] forbidden relations, one awake and one sleeping, the one sleeping is exempt.

messages.caption: The baraita taught before Rav Sheshet: each “they rendered … like …,” why it fails as plainly read, and how Rav Sheshet reads it, every line resting on “lies carnally.”

messages.text: It has been determined that one who engages in intercourse intentionally or engages in the initial stage of intercourse with an espoused maidservant is like one who does so unintentionally with all those with whom relations are forbidden, meaning that he is exempt.

notes.he: שהערה בה בכוונה פטור דהעראה בשפחה פטור כשאינו מתכוין דעריות. העראה פלוגתא היא (בסנהדרין בארבע מיתות) (סנהדרין דף נה:) איכא למ"ד העראה זו נשיקה ואיכא למאן דאמר זו הכנסת עטרה:
notes.en: It is found that one who intends and engages in the initial stage with the maidservant: one who engaged in the initial stage with her intentionally is exempt, for the initial stage with the maidservant is exempt; [he is] like one who does not intend with forbidden relations. [What] the initial stage [is] is a matter of dispute (in Sanhedrin, in the chapter Arba Mitot, 55b): there is one who says the initial stage is the touching [lit. kissing] [of the organs], and there is one who says it is the insertion of the corona.

notes.he: קשה אמאי האריך הש"ס בלישניה דהאי לאו פירוש דברייתא הוא דכבר אסיקנא ליה שפיר:
notes.en: It is found that one who intends, etc.: It is difficult: why did the Gemara lengthen its language? For this is not an explanation of the baraita, since we have already concluded it well.

notes.he: פירש הקונטרס כגון שאשתו ואחותו במטה וכסבור לבא על אשתו ונמצא אחותו דפטור ממלקות וחייב חטאת הואיל ונהנה דמתעסק הוא וקשה שהרי בשפחה נמי חייב חטאת בכי האי גוונא שהרי מביאין על הזדון כשוגג וא"כ מאי קאמר נמצא מתכוין בשפחה כשאין מתכוין לעריות בכה"ג שוו תרווייהו לכך יש לומר כשאין מתכוין דעריות כגון נפל מן הגג ונתקע דפטור לגמרי דאנוס הוא:
notes.en: Like one who does not intend with forbidden relations: The Kuntres [Rashi] explained: for example, where his wife and his sister were in the bed, and he thought to have intercourse with his wife and it turned out to be his sister, where he is exempt from lashes and liable to a sin offering since he derived pleasure, for he is one who acts unawares [mitasek]. But this is difficult: for with the maidservant too he is liable to an offering in such a case, since one brings [the offering] for the intentional as for the unwitting [the Hebrew says “sin offering”; for the maidservant the mishna’s offering is a guilt offering]. If so, what does it mean: one who intends with the maidservant is found to be like one who does not intend with forbidden relations? In such a case the two are equal! Therefore one may say: like one who does not intend with forbidden relations, for example one who fell from a roof and was thrust in, who is entirely exempt, for he is a victim of circumstance.

messages.text: Similarly, one who engages in intercourse with an espoused maidservant in a typical manner while sleeping is like one who does so, while sleeping, with all those others with whom relations are forbidden, and he is likewise exempt. Furthermore, it has also been determined that one who engages in atypical intercourse with an espoused maidservant while awake is like one who does so with all those with whom relations are forbidden, while sleeping, and he is also exempt.

notes.he: ונמצא ניעור וגומר שלא כדרכה בשפחה דפטור כישן דכל עריות ופטור דעריות לא הוי אלא אין מתכוין כדאמרן וישן אבל מתכוין שלא כדרכה חייב בעריות דלא כתיב בהו אשה שכבת. והשתא מתרצו להו עשו גומר כמערה כולהו מעריות לפטורה:
notes.en: And it is found that one who is awake and completes atypical [intercourse] with a maidservant is exempt, like one sleeping with all forbidden relations. And the exemption with forbidden relations exists only [for] one who does not intend, as we said, and one who is sleeping; but one who intends atypical [intercourse] is liable with forbidden relations, for “lies carnally” is not written with regard to them. And now they resolve them all, “they rendered one who completes like one who engages in the initial stage,” [as comparisons] to the exemption of forbidden relations.

notes.he: סליק פירקא
notes.en: The chapter is concluded.

messages.text: הדרן עלך ארבעה מחוסרי כפרה · Hadran alakh Arba’a Meḥusarei Kappara: we will return to you, chapter 2, “Four Who Lack Atonement.”
Chapter 3 · אמרו לו · Amru Lo: testimony that a person ate forbidden fat, and when eating forbidden foods in one lapse of awareness brings one sin offering or several.
Mishna
If witnesses said to a person: We saw that you ate forbidden fat, he is liable to bring a sin offering if he did so unwittingly.

notes.he: מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: Mishna. They said to him: it is explained in the Gemara.

notes.dh: מתני' אמרו לו עד אומר לו אכל כו'
notes.he: צ"ל דמיירי שהעידוהו שנים בבת אחת דאי בזה אחר זה הא כ"מ שהאמינה תורה עד אחד הרי כאן שנים וכיון שנתקבל עדותו תו לא קפדינן בעדות השני שאומר לא אכל וצ"ל דמיירי שהאיש שמעידין בו שותק דאי אמר איני יודע פטור כדנפקא בגמרא או הודע אליו כו' ומסיק דמיירי בעד אחד שאינו יכול לחייבו קרבן וע"כ מיירי שאותו שהעיד עליו אומר איני יודע דאי אמר לא אכלתי פשיטא דעד אחד לא מהימן כדכתיב (דברים יט) לא יקום עד אחד באיש דנראה שאין עד אחד קם רק לשבועה:
notes.en: Mishna. They said to him… a witness says: He ate, etc.: It must be that [the mishna] speaks where [the two] testified about him at the same time; for if one after the other, then wherever the Torah deemed one witness credible, he is [as good as] two, and once his testimony was accepted we no longer pay attention to the testimony of the second, who says: He did not eat. And it must be that it speaks where the man about whom they testify is silent; for if he said: I do not know, he is exempt, as is derived in the Gemara from “or if [his sin] is known to him,” etc. And [the Gemara] concludes that it speaks of one witness, who cannot render him liable to bring an offering, and necessarily it speaks where the one about whom he testified says: I do not know; for if he said: I did not eat, it is obvious that one witness is not credible, as it is written: “One witness shall not rise up against a man” (Deuteronomy 19:15), from which it appears that one witness rises only for an oath.

notes.he: כזית מביא חטאת:
notes.en: They said to him, two [witnesses]: You ate forbidden fat: an olive-bulk, he brings a sin offering.

messages.text: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and a witness says: He did not eat forbidden fat, or if a woman says: He ate forbidden fat, and a woman says: He did not eat forbidden fat, he is liable to bring a provisional guilt offering, brought by one who is uncertain as to whether he committed a sin that requires a sin offering.

notes.he: מכאן משמע דאשה מהימנא טפי מגזלן שהרי גבי גזלן משמע דלא אמרי' שתיקה כהודאה כדאמרינן (קדושין דף סו.) אי מהימנא לך דלא גזלנא הוא זיל אפקה ואע"ג דשתקה אלמא לא אמרינן שתיקה כהודאה דמיא ועובדא הוה ההוא סמיא דהוה מסדר מתנייתא קמי דרב ששת כו' אתא חד גברא ואמר שאשתו זינתה וקא אמר אי מהימנא לך דלאו גזלנא הוא זיל אפקה והכא אי שתיק מהימנא האשה:
notes.en: And a woman says: He did not eat: From here it is implied that a woman is more credible than a robber; for with regard to a robber it is implied that we do not say silence is like admission, as we say (Kiddushin 66a): “If he is credible to you that he is not a robber, go divorce her,” even though she was silent; evidently we do not say that silence is like admission. And the incident was: that blind man who would arrange mishnayot before Rav Sheshet, etc.; a certain man came and said that [the blind man’s] wife had committed adultery, and he said: If he is credible to you that he is not a robber, go divorce her. And here, if he is silent, the woman is believed.

notes.dh: עד אומר אכל כו' מביא אשם תלוי
notes.he: דספק הוא הואיל ומכחיש זה את זה ובהא עדות אשה נאמנת דמרבי לה בספרא מן או דכתיב או הודע אליו מ"מ:
notes.en: A witness says: He ate, etc., he brings a provisional guilt offering: for it is uncertain, since they contradict each other. And in this a woman’s testimony is credible, for it is included in the Sifra from “or,” as it is written: “Or if [his sin] is known to him,” in any case.

messages.text: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself says: I did not eat forbidden fat, he is exempt.

notes.dh: עד אומר אכל והוא אומר לא אכלתי פטור
notes.he: והוא הדין אם אמר איני יודע כמו שפירשתי:
notes.en: A witness says: He ate, and he says: I did not eat, he is exempt: And the same is true if he said: I do not know, as I explained.

notes.dh: עד אחד אומר אכל והוא אומר לא אכלתי
notes.he: פטור מקרבן דהא אדם נאמן על עצמו בדבר שצריך כפרה יותר ממאה עדים דהכי אמרינן בגמרא דהכי סבירא להו לרבנן וכ"ש הכא דליכא אלא עד אחד:
notes.en: One witness says: He ate, and he says: I did not eat: he is exempt from an offering, for a person is believed about himself, in a matter that requires atonement, more than a hundred witnesses, for so we say in the Gemara that this is the view of the Rabbis; and all the more so here, where there is only one witness.

messages.text: If two witnesses say: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself says: I did not eat forbidden fat, Rabbi Meir deems him liable to bring a sin offering.

This conclusion can be derived a fortiori: If two witnesses could have brought him liability to receive the severe punishment of death, can they not bring him liability to sacrifice an offering, which is relatively lenient?

notes.he: כגון אם העידו בו שהרג את הנפש:
notes.en: If [two] brought him, etc.: for example, if they testified about him that he killed a person.

notes.he: שאם העידהו בדבר שחייב מיתה ממיתין אותו על פיהן ואעפ"י אם מכחישן הוא לא יביאהו לקרבן הקל שהוא קל לגבי מיתה ואע"ג דמכחישן הוא:
notes.en: If two brought him to death: for if they testified about him in a matter for which he is liable to death, they execute him on their word even though he contradicts them; shall they not bring him to an offering, which is lenient compared to death, even though he contradicts them?

messages.text: @Rabbi Meir Witnesses are unable to render another person liable to bring an offering contrary to his statement, as what if he wishes to say: I did so intentionally, in which case he would be exempt from bringing an offering?
messages.quote: can they not bring him liability to sacrifice an offering

notes.he: אם היה רוצה לפטור עצמו בשקר היה יכול לומר מזיד היה ומזיד פטור:
notes.en: If he wishes to say: I acted intentionally: if he wished to exempt himself with a lie, he could say he acted intentionally, and one who acts intentionally is exempt [from an offering].

notes.he: לא אלא פטור הוא שזה שהוא אומר לא אכלתי אינו מכחישן שאם ירצה יאמר לא אכלתי שוגג אלא מזיד ומזיד פטור מקרבן ומתוך שיכול לומר כן כשאמר לא אכלתי פטור:
notes.en: They said to him: No; rather, he is exempt, for this one who says “I did not eat” is not [really] contradicting them, for if he wishes he can say: I did not eat unwittingly but intentionally, and one who acts intentionally is exempt from an offering. And since he can say this, when he said “I did not eat,” he is exempt.

messages.text: If one unwittingly ate an olive-bulk of forbidden fat and then ate another olive-bulk of forbidden fat during one lapse of awareness, i.e., in a case where he did not discover in the interim that fat is forbidden, or that the food he is eating is forbidden fat, he is liable to bring only one sin offering.

If one ate forbidden fat, and blood, and piggul, and notar in one lapse of awareness, he is liable to bring a sin offering for each and every one of them. This is a stringency that applies to one who eats several types of forbidden food and does not apply to one who eats one type of forbidden food.

And a stringency that applies to one who eats one type of forbidden food and not to one who eats several types of forbidden food is that if one ate half an olive-bulk and then ate another half an olive-bulk during one lapse of awareness, in a case where they were both from one type of forbidden food, he is liable to bring a sin offering. If they were from two types, he is exempt, because he did not eat an olive-bulk of any specific forbidden food.

notes.dh: שאם אכל כחצי זית וחזר ואכל כחצי זית ממין אחד חייב משני מינין פטור
notes.he: וא"ת והא אמרינן בפ' קדשי מזבח (מעילה יז:) הפיגול והנותר אין מצטרפין וקא אמר בגמרא לא שנו אלא לטומאת ידים אבל לאכילה מצטרפין וי"ל דהתם לענין מלקות אי נמי לענין שאם יפלו לקדירה אחת מצטרפין לתת טעם דהא שם אחד הוא דליכא אלא חד לאו אתרווייהו אבל הכא מיירי לדין חיוב קרבן:
notes.en: For if he ate half an olive-bulk and again ate half an olive-bulk from one type, he is liable; from two types, he is exempt: And if you say: But we say in the chapter Kodshei Mizbe’aḥ (Me’ila 17b): Piggul and notar do not combine, and it says in the Gemara: They taught this only with regard to impurity of the hands, but for eating they combine? One may say that there it is with regard to lashes; alternatively, with regard to where they fell into one pot, they combine to impart flavor, since it is one name, for there is only one prohibition for both; but here it speaks of the law of liability to an offering.

messages.caption: The mishna’s cases of testimony that a person ate forbidden fat, and what each one obligates him to bring.

messages.text: Gemara

The mishna teaches: If witnesses said to him: You ate forbidden fat, he is liable to bring a sin offering. Since the mishna employs the plural form of the word said, how many witnesses are involved in the case? There must be at least two witnesses.
messages.quote: you ate forbidden fat, he is liable to bring a sin offering

messages.text: And what does he say to them in response? If we say that he is silent and does not contradict them, then it may be inferred that it is only when he responds with silence in response to the claim of two witnesses that he brings a sin offering, but for silence in response to the claim of one witness, he does not bring a sin offering.

But say the middle clause: If a witness says that he ate forbidden fat, and the person himself says: I did not eat it, he is exempt. The reason that he is exempt is that he contradicts him. But if he is silent, he is liable, and all the more so if he is silent when two witnesses claim that he ate forbidden fat. This contradicts the inference from the first clause that silence in response to one witness does not render one liable to bring a sin offering.
messages.quote: and the person himself says: I did not eat forbidden fat, he is exempt

notes.dh: אימא מציעתא עד אומר אכל והוא אומר לא אכלתי כו'
notes.he: והוא הדין דמצי מייתי מרישא עד אומר אכל ועד אומר לא אכל ומביא אשם תלוי טעמא דאמר עד אחד לא אכל הא לאו הכי חייב חטאת דשתיקה כהודאה דמיא דע"כ מיירי דשתק דאי מכחיש ליה פטור לגמרי ואפילו אומר איני יודע כמו שפירשתי:
notes.en: Say the middle clause: A witness says he ate, and he says: I did not eat, etc.: And the same is so, that it could have brought [the inference] from the first clause: A witness says he ate and a witness says he did not eat, and he brings a provisional guilt offering. The reason is that one witness said he did not eat; but otherwise he would be liable to a sin offering, for silence is like admission. For necessarily it speaks where he was silent, for if he contradicted him he would be entirely exempt, and even if he says: I do not know, as I explained.

notes.he: אבל שתיק מישתק לחד מיחייב קרבן וכ"ש כי שתיק לתרי דמיחייב קרבן והאי ממציעתא מצינן למידק ולא איצטריך למימר רישא:
notes.en: But [if] he is silent, [when] silent to one [witness] he is liable to an offering, and all the more so when he is silent to two, that he is liable to an offering; and this we can infer from the middle clause, and the first clause did not need to be stated.

messages.text: Rather, the first clause is referring to a case where he contradicts the claim of the two witnesses. Whose opinion is this? It is that of Rabbi Meir, who says in the continuation of the mishna that the person’s contradiction of the testimony of two witnesses is not considered a contradiction, and he is liable to bring a sin offering. But according to the opinion of the Rabbis, he is exempt.

notes.he: דאמר אם הביאוהו שנים כו':
notes.en: Gemara. It is Rabbi Meir: who said: If two brought him, etc.

notes.dh: אלא דקא מכחיש להו ומני ר"מ היא
notes.he: דליכא למימר דמיירי כשאמר איני יודע דפשיטא דחייב דאיני יודע גבי תרי עדים הויא כשתיקה:
notes.en: Rather, where he contradicts them, and whose is it? It is Rabbi Meir: for one cannot say it speaks where he said: I do not know, since [then] it is obvious that he is liable, for “I do not know” in the face of two witnesses is like silence.

notes.he: ברישא ואפי' הכי מביא חטאת ומני ר' מאיר דאמר הכחשה כו':
notes.en: Rather, where he contradicts them: in the first clause, and even so he brings a sin offering. And whose is it? Rabbi Meir’s, who says: [the] contradiction, etc.

notes.he: היינו סיפא:
notes.en: But according to the Rabbis he is exempt: that is the latter clause.

messages.text: And according to this answer, what does the tanna teach us in the first clause? From the latter clause you already learn that according to Rabbi Meir, one is liable to bring a sin offering as a result of the testimony of two witnesses, even if he contradicts them.

notes.dh: מאי קמשמע לן הא מסיפא שמעינן לה
notes.he: דקתני שנים אומרים אכל כו':
notes.en: What does it teach us? We learn it from the latter clause: which teaches: Two say he ate, etc.

messages.text: The latter clause is clarifying the first clause, and this is what it teaches us: This matter that was stated in the first clause is actually the subject of a dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis, and that dispute pertains to a case where he contradicts their testimony.

notes.he: ששנינו למעלה אמרו לו אכלת כו' מביא חטאת לאו דברי הכל היא אלא מחלוקת ר"מ וחכמים שרבי מאיר אומר אם הביאוהו שנים כו' וחכמים אומרים כו' וסיפא מפרש לרישא:
notes.en: This is what it is saying: the latter clause [teaches that] this matter that we learned above, “They said to him: You ate, etc., he brings a sin offering,” is not the statement of all; rather, it is a dispute of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis, for Rabbi Meir says: If two brought him, etc., and the Rabbis say, etc.; and the latter clause explains the first clause.

notes.he: תימה למאי איצטריך למיסתמיה ברישא אי דליהוי סתם ואחר כך מחלוקת פשיטא דיחיד ורבים הלכה כרבים:
notes.en: This matter is a dispute between Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis: It is puzzling: for what purpose was it necessary to state it anonymously in the first clause? If so that it should be an anonymous [ruling] followed by a dispute, it is obvious, for [between] an individual and the many, the halakha follows the many.

messages.text: The case is where only one witness asserts that the individual ate forbidden fat, and occasionally the plural verb form in the expression: Witnesses said to him, can also be used to refer to one witness.
messages.lead: Some say a different explanation of the first clause:

notes.he: הכי פריך הש"ס אמרו משמע חד כו':
notes.en: Some say: the Gemara asks thus: “they said” implies even one, etc.

messages.text: With regard to a woman whose husband went overseas, and witnesses came and said to her: Your husband died, and she married another man on the basis of this testimony, and afterward her husband came back, she must leave both this man, her first husband, and that one, whom she married subsequently.

This mishna indicates that the plural expression can be used in the case of a single witness, as we maintain that this mishna is referring even to a case where one witness testified that her husband died.

From where is this inferred? It is inferred from the fact that the latter clause of that mishna teaches: If she married without consent and then her first husband returned, she is permitted to return to him.
messages.quote: came and said to her: Your husband died

messages.text: What does the mishna mean when it states that she remarried without consent? It means she remarried without the consent of the court, which would be granted based on the testimony of one witness. Rather, two witnesses testified that her husband had died. Since that is full-fledged halakhic testimony, she is permitted to remarry independently, even without the explicit consent of the court.

notes.he: לראשון ועל פי עדים שאמרו לה שנים מת בעליך ולפיכך מותרת לראשון שהרי אנוסה היא ששנים אמרו לה דאונס בישראל שרי:
notes.en: She is permitted to return to him: to the first, and [this is] on the basis of witnesses, two of whom said to her: Your husband died. Therefore she is permitted to the first, for she acted under duress, since two said it to her, and [a wife who acted under] duress remains permitted to an Israelite [husband who is not a priest].

notes.he: אין הכי נמי אלא הא קמ"ל רישא כי קא מכחיש להון דדבר זה היינו מחלוקת ר' מאיר ורבנן בסיפא. וק"ל דאפי' בחד קאמר. ובאו ואמרו לה. נישאת שלא ברשות ב"ד שלא הוצרכה לטול רשות מב"ד מפני שניסת על פי שנים עדים מותרת לחזור לו דאינו דומה לנבעלת לרצון דאסורה לבעלה אלא הויא כי נבעלת באונס דמאי הוה לה למידק תו מאחר שאמרו לה ב' עדים מת בעליך:
notes.en: Indeed so; but this is what the first clause teaches us: where he contradicts them, that this matter is the dispute of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis in the latter clause. And [the second version] holds that [“they said”] is said even of one. “And [witnesses] came and said to her”: [if] she married without the consent of the court, for she did not need to take permission from the court, since she married on the basis of two witnesses, she is permitted to return to him; for she is not like one who had intercourse willingly, who is forbidden to her husband, but is like one who had intercourse under duress. For what more should she have investigated, after two witnesses said to her: Your husband died?

messages.text: By inference, one may conclude that the first clause is referring to a case where she married with the consent of the court and on the basis of the testimony of one witness. Evidently, that mishna teaches the plural form of the word: Said, when it is referring to one witness, and here, too, in this mishna where it teaches the phrase: Witnesses said to him, it indicates that even one witness renders one liable to bring a sin offering.

notes.he: דקתני תצא מזה ומזה שנשאת ברשות ב"ד ועד אחד דהוה לה למידק יפה אם מת דהאי דשריוה רבנן לאנסובי על פי עד אחד משום דדייקא ומנסבא דמתוך חומר שהחמרת עליה בסופה דתצא מזה ומזה הקלת עליה בתחלתה כדאמר במסכת יבמות (דף פח.) ואמטו להכי נשאת על פי עד אחד והיא גופה לא דייקא ואישתכח דלא מת תצא מזה ומזה כדאמרינן במסכת סוטה (דף כז:) ונטמאה ונטמאה שני פעמים אחד לבעל ואחד לבועל:
notes.en: By inference, the first clause: which teaches “she must leave this one and that one,” [is a case] where she married with the consent of the court and on the basis of one witness, for she should have investigated carefully whether he had died. For the reason the Rabbis permitted her to marry on the basis of one witness is that she investigates carefully and [only then] marries, since by the stringency you imposed on her at the end, that she must leave this one and that one, you were lenient with her at the beginning, as said in tractate Yevamot (88a). Therefore, [where] she married on the basis of one witness and did not herself investigate, and it turned out that he had not died, she must leave this one and that one, as we say in tractate Sota (27b): “And she was defiled… and she was defiled,” twice: once [forbidding her] to the husband and once to the paramour.

notes.dh: מכלל דרישא ברשות ב"ד ועד אחד
notes.he: דבשני עדים אין צריך רשות ב"ד:
notes.en: By inference, the first clause is with the consent of the court and one witness: for with two witnesses there is no need for the consent of the court.

notes.he: מכלל דרישא דקתני תצא מזה ומזה כגון דנשאת ברשות שלא היה לה אלא עד אחד והוצרכה ליטול רשות מב"ד לינשא ואמאי אסורה לבעלה דהויא כי נבעלת ברצון לאחר דהוה לה דלא תינשא אלא ע"פ שנים אלמא האי ואמרו לה דרישא עד אחד הוא:
notes.en: By inference, the first clause, which teaches “she must leave this one and that one,” [is] where she married with consent, having had only one witness, and needed to take permission from the court to marry. And why is she forbidden to her husband? For she is like one who had intercourse willingly with another, since she should not have married except on the basis of two. Evidently this “and they said to her” of the first clause is one witness.

messages.text: And what does he say in response to the witness? If we say that he contradicts the witness, does he bring an offering? But doesn’t the middle clause teach: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself says: I did not eat forbidden fat, he is exempt?
messages.quote: and the person himself says: I did not eat forbidden fat, he is exempt

messages.text: Rather, if it is referring to a case where he is silent, the clause is unnecessary, as one can learn this halakha from the middle clause, which states: If a witness says: He ate forbidden fat, and the person himself says: I did not eat forbidden fat, he is exempt from bringing a sin offering. This indicates that the reason he is exempt is that he contradicts the witness, but if he was silent, he is liable to bring a sin offering.

notes.he: סוף סוף מאי קמ"ל רישא הא מן מצעתא שמעינן מינה:
notes.en: After all, what does the first clause teach us? We learn it from the middle clause.

messages.text: Actually, the first clause of the mishna is referring to a case where he does not contradict the witness but remains silent. And this is what the mishna is teaching: If they, i.e., even one witness, said to him: You ate forbidden fat, he is liable to bring a sin offering. The middle clause then clarifies: In what case is this statement said? It is said where he was silent in response to this accusation, but if he contradicts the witness, he is exempt.

notes.he: ומתניתין הכי קתני אמרו לו [כו'] בד"א בשותק אבל מכחישו כגון עד אמר אכל והוא אמר לא אכלתי פטור:
notes.en: Actually, where he does not contradict him: and our mishna teaches thus: “They said to him, etc.” In what case is this said? Where he is silent; but if he contradicts him, for example a witness said he ate and he said: I did not eat, he is exempt.

notes.he: כדקתני במציעתא פטור:
notes.en: Actually, where he does not contradict him [an editor suggests reading: and so it teaches: They said to him, etc. In what case is this said? Where he is silent; but if he contradicts him, it teaches in the middle clause that he is exempt]: as it teaches in the middle clause: exempt.

messages.text: And from where do we derive that by Torah law that if he does not contradict the witness, he is liable to bring a sin offering?

“Or if his sin is known to him” (Leviticus 4:28), that this is referring to a case where he found out himself but not a case where others informed him of his sin. One might have thought he is exempt even if he does not contradict the claim of the witness. Therefore, the verse states: “Or if his sin is known to him,” which teaches that in any case where he knows that he sinned, even if others informed him of it, he is liable. He is exempt only if he denies it.
messages.lead: It is as the Sages taught in a baraita with regard to a verse that deals with a sin offering:

verse.he: אוֹ הוֹדַע אֵלָיו חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא וְהֵבִיא קׇרְבָּנוֹ שְׂעִירַת עִזִּים תְּמִימָה נְקֵבָה עַל־חַטָּאתוֹ אֲשֶׁר חָטָא׃
verse.en: or the sin of which they are guilty is made known—that person shall bring a female goat without blemish as an offering for the aforementioned sin.

notes.he: משמע מעצמו ולא שיודיעוהו אחרים:
notes.en: Is known to him: implies of his own accord, and not that others inform him.

notes.he: היה יכול לומר או הודע לו והיה משמע הודע לו שהודיעוהו אחרים מאי הודע אליו שצריך שתהא הודעה אליו כלומר שצריך שיזכר אליו כשהזכירוהו אבל אם מכחישו פטור:
notes.en: As the Sages taught: “Or if [his sin] is known to him [hoda elav]”: it could have said “or if it is known to him [hoda lo],” which would imply that it was made known to him, that others informed him. What [is meant by] “hoda elav”? That the knowledge must be to him, that is, that he must recall it when they remind him; but if he contradicts him, he is exempt.

notes.he: ואמרינן התם בסיפרא יכול אפי' אין מכחישו אלא שותק כשיאמר לו עד אחד אכל חלב יהא פטור ת"ל או הודע מכל מקום בין בעד אחד בין ע"פ קרוב בין ע"פ אשה ואינו מכחישו חייב:
notes.en: And we say there in the Sifra: I might think that even [if] he does not contradict him but is silent, when one witness says to him: He ate forbidden fat, he would be exempt; the verse states: “Or if it is known,” in any case: whether by one witness, or by a relative, or by a woman, and he does not contradict him, he is liable.

messages.text: What are we dealing with, in the case where he is informed by others? If we say that it is referring to two witnesses who inform him, in a case where two witnesses testify and he does not contradict them does one need a verse to render him liable?
messages.quote: where others informed him of his sin

messages.text: Continues on 12a: rather, the baraita must be referring to one witness, and it teaches that when the person does not contradict him, the witness is deemed credible; one witness can render a person liable to bring a sin offering.
